subject: How to insert a genetic map of one cross object to another?

messages.author: ae4e3267fde51265
messages.subject: How to insert a genetic map of one cross object to another?
parts:
Dr. Broman, 

I have created a genetic map for the males in my dataset, but I need to use the same genetic map for the female sample. Is there a way to insert the genetic map from the males into the female cross object? The male map is not the same length as the female sample's but it has the same marker names. Thank you for your help!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to insert a genetic map of one cross object to another?
parts:
Could you show the code that you’re using?

From the error message, it seems like you’re calling replace.map(map_athaf2, nm2) but from the name “map_athaf2” that sounds like a map not a cross object.

If you want to insert the female map into the male cross, you should call replace.map() with the male cross and the female map, and what you’ll get as output is the male cross with its map replaced with the female one.

female_map <- pull.map(female_cross)
male_map_with_female_cross <- replace.map(male_cross, female_map)

karl

On Feb 24, 2019, at 1:38 PM, Julie Kim <julie...@gmail.com> wrote:

I tried using the replace.map() function but it keeps giving me this error even though I made sure all the markers from the female map were the same ones (same name and same amount of markers) as the ones in the male map. I am trying to replace the female map in the female cross object with the re-estimated new male map. Do you have any ideas as to why this may be happening? Thank you so much!

2.
replacemap.cross(cross, map)
1.

On Sunday, February 24, 2019 at 3:36:30 PM UTC-5, Karl Broman wrote:
Could you show the code that you’re using?

From the error message, it seems like you’re calling replace.map(map_athaf2, nm2) but from the name “map_athaf2” that sounds like a map not a cross object.

If you want to insert the female map into the male cross, you should call replace.map() with the male cross and the female map, and what you’ll get as output is the male cross with its map replaced with the female one.

female_map <- pull.map(female_cross)
male_map_with_female_cross <- replace.map(male_cross, female_map)

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to insert a genetic map of one cross object to another?
parts:
You could use the function movemarker(), moving the markers one at a time to the position in the female map. Something like this:

female_map <- pull.map(map_athaf2)
for(chr in names(female_map)) {
    pos <- female_map[[chr]]
    markers <- names(pos)
    for(i in seq_along(pos) {
        map_atham2 <- movemarker(map_atham2, markers[i], chr, pos[i])
    }
}

karl
